A model is a set of choices.

CH7-01 · Reproduce a compound path and identify the assumptions that created it.

A simulation calculates consequences of a specified model using repeatable pseudo-random draws. It does not turn assumptions into market evidence. Our original model starts at £100 and takes three hypothetical periods. Each period independently draws one of −a%, 0%, +a%, each with probability 1/3. The spread a is 5, 10 or 20. These are percentage returns, not price changes in pounds.

Next price = current price × (1 + return / 100)

Worked example with a=10: +10%, 0%, −10% gives £100→£110→£110→£99. The arithmetic mean return is zero, but the compounded change is −1%. Predict before calculating: do opposite returns cancel? Their multiplication, 1.1×.9=.99, shows they do not.

The model assumes independent draws, equal probabilities, a fixed distribution and no prices below zero. It bounds one-period losses to a%, excludes jumps beyond its three allowed outcomes, and omits taxes, trading, dividends and volatility clustering. Three model periods are not labelled years or days: no annualised forecast is implied. Change one assumption deliberately; log it even when the result looks worse.

Guided practice:attempt before feedback

  1. A three-period path starts at £100, then returns +10%, 0%, −10%. Terminal price (£)?

    My calculation and units:________

    Hint,answer and revision feedback

    99;100 × 1.10 × 1 × .90 = 99. If your method differs,identify the assumption or arithmetic error,recalculate and record the correction.

  2. In the stated equally likely three-point model, one-period probability of a negative return (0–1)?

    My calculation and units:________

    Hint,answer and revision feedback

    0.3333333333333333;Only one of −10%, 0%, +10% is negative. This is a model input, not an estimated market fact. If your method differs,identify the assumption or arithmetic error,recalculate and record the correction.

Show one compounded path and explain why equal model probabilities and bounded outcomes are assumptions rather than measured market facts. Write30+characters with a checked number.

Self-review:I used multiplication and named independence, bounded tails and fixed probabilities. Revise any unmet criterion before proceeding.

Commit to buy. Keep both directions.

CH7-02 · Calculate the terminal payoff of one long forward unit.

A simplified long forward commits to buy one unit at a fixed delivery price K on the terminal date. At that date the asset is worth ST. The economic payoff is ST−K. A low terminal price produces a negative payoff: the obligation does not disappear.

Long forward terminal payoff = ST − K

Worked K=100: if terminal price is £120 the payoff is +£20; at £90 it is −£10; at £100 it is zero. Predict: is a forward floor of zero correct? No: that floor describes optional exercise for a call, not a binding long forward.

There is no initial premium, margin, financing, counterparty default or discounting in this teaching example. We calculate terminal payoff only; we are not determining a fair forward price. Real contracts can require collateral and involve credit or funding costs. Units are pounds per one underlying unit, never percentage investment returns.

Guided practice:attempt before feedback

  1. Long forward, K=100, terminal price=90. Payoff (£ per unit)?

    My calculation and units:________

    Hint,answer and revision feedback

    -10;90 − 100 = −10. A long forward can have a negative payoff. If your method differs,identify the assumption or arithmetic error,recalculate and record the correction.

  2. New case: K=95, terminal price=112. Long forward payoff (£)?

    My calculation and units:________

    Hint,answer and revision feedback

    17;112 − 95 = 17. There is no initial premium in this simplified example. If your method differs,identify the assumption or arithmetic error,recalculate and record the correction.

Compare terminal prices below and above strike. State the obligation, units and exclusions; do not call the positive side a guarantee. Write30+characters with a checked number.

Self-review:I kept negative forward payoffs and distinguished payoff from return and contract pricing. Revise any unmet criterion before proceeding.

The right has a price.

CH7-03 · Distinguish a call’s terminal payoff from undiscounted profit after premium.

A long call gives the right to buy one unit at strike K on the terminal date. The holder can choose not to exercise. Therefore payoff is max(ST−K,0). The premium is paid for this right and is excluded from payoff. To calculate our simplified undiscounted profit, subtract the premium once.

Call payoff = max(ST − K, 0)
Undiscounted profit = call payoff − premium

Worked K=100, premium £6: terminal £90 gives payoff £0 and profit −£6. Terminal £104 gives payoff £4 and profit −£2. Terminal £120 gives payoff £20 and profit £14. Predict: does finishing above strike guarantee profit? No: the payoff first has to recover the premium. Break-even is £106 under these assumptions.

The £6 premium is supplied, not priced by this simulation. We deliberately ignore the time value of money, so subtracting an earlier premium from terminal cash is an undiscounted teaching convention. Financing or discounting would change the economic comparison. No option-pricing derivation, early exercise, dividends, fees, taxes or hedging is assessed.

Guided practice:attempt before feedback

  1. Call strike £100, premium £6, terminal £104. Payoff (£)?

    My calculation and units:________

    Hint,answer and revision feedback

    4;max(104−100,0)=4. Premium is not subtracted from payoff. If your method differs,identify the assumption or arithmetic error,recalculate and record the correction.

  2. Same call: terminal £104. Undiscounted profit (£)?

    My calculation and units:________

    Hint,answer and revision feedback

    -2;Payoff 4 minus premium 6 = −2. In-the-money is not necessarily profitable. If your method differs,identify the assumption or arithmetic error,recalculate and record the correction.

Give a terminal price where the call is in the money but makes a loss. Distinguish pounds of payoff, premium and undiscounted profit. Write30+characters with a checked number.

Self-review:I subtract premium once from payoff and disclose the no-discounting convention. Revise any unmet criterion before proceeding.

Separate precision from credibility.

CH7-04 · Interpret simulated outcome counts without treating the model as a forecast.

A 100-path sample has sampling variation even when its generator is fixed. Reporting “37 of 100 calls made a profit” describes this run, conditional on its assumptions. It does not establish a 37% future market probability. Repeating the same seed exactly reproduces the path list; changing the seed changes draws, not the underlying assumptions.

More paths can reduce random simulation noise around this chosen model’s outputs. They cannot verify equal probabilities, independence, missing tail events or a fixed distribution. Predict: if we widen a from 10 to 20 with the seed fixed, will the signs of the individual returns change? No: the same draw chooses down, zero or up; only their size changes. Terminal outcomes and derivative payoffs can change nonlinearly.

For a=10, a three-down path is £100×.9³=£72.90. For a=20 it is £51.20. The model still excludes outcomes below that floor; markets do not promise such a bound. A minimum among simulated paths is neither a market worst case nor a risk guarantee. Review every path in the table rather than relying on an average alone.

Guided practice:attempt before feedback

  1. Call strike £100, premium £6. Terminal break-even price (£), ignoring financing?

    My calculation and units:________

    Hint,answer and revision feedback

    106;At 106, payoff is 6 and profit is zero. If your method differs,identify the assumption or arithmetic error,recalculate and record the correction.

  2. Enter 1: more paths validate the return assumptions; 2: more paths describe the chosen model more precisely.

    My calculation and units:________

    Hint,answer and revision feedback

    2;Choose 2. Simulation precision cannot validate a model against markets. If your method differs,identify the assumption or arithmetic error,recalculate and record the correction.

Explain a fixed-seed, changed-spread comparison and name a risk excluded by the model. Separate numerical reproducibility from external validity. Write30+characters with a checked number.

Self-review:I described conditional results and rejected forecast or worst-case guarantees. Revise any unmet criterion before proceeding.

Starting100,compound three returns(direction×spread%) per path,then continue draws for100paths. Independent bounded equally likely draws and a fixed distribution are model assumptions,not financial evidence.

Hand-check and feedback

Seed42first directions are down,down,zero. Spread10:100×.9×.9×1=81;spread20:100×.8×.8×1=64. Larger steps do not make every terminal outcome higher. Calls have payoffmax(terminal−100,0),profitpayoff−6. More paths cannot validate equal probabilities,independence or missing tails. A model minimum is not a market worst-case guarantee.

Write a50+character comparison naming observed outcomes and assumptions. Correct one forecast-like claim. Keep every run,including disappointing ones,on paper.

Independent transfer20min

Attempt all8before revealing feedback. Meet at least7/8and every critical item;there is no reward for positive returns. This is formative self-learning,not a secure exam. Then write a specific30+character response to feedback,correct errors and resubmit on paper with a new dated attempt. Retain every attempt.

  1. New path: £80 ×1.20 ×0.80. Terminal price (£)?

    My method and answer:________

  2. Long forward K=80, terminal £76.80. Payoff (£)? Critical

    My method and answer:________

  3. Call K=80, premium £5, terminal £76.80. Payoff (£)? Critical

    My method and answer:________

  4. That call’s undiscounted profit (£)? Critical

    My method and answer:________

  5. Call K=80, premium £5, terminal £84. Profit (£)?

    My method and answer:________

  6. Call K=80, premium £5. Break-even terminal (£)?

    My method and answer:________

  7. Enter 1: a seeded model is a guaranteed forecast; 2: outcomes are conditional on its assumptions. Critical

    My method and answer:________

  8. Enter 1: repeat the same seed and assumptions to reproduce; 2: choose a different seed to guarantee identical paths.

    My method and answer:________

Answer feedback:open after attempting all8
  1. a1:76.8. 80×1.2×.8=76.8.
  2. a2:-3.2. 76.8−80=−3.2.
  3. a3:0. Exercise is optional: max(76.8−80,0)=0.
  4. a4:-5. 0 payoff minus 5 premium.
  5. a5:-1. Payoff 4 minus premium 5.
  6. a6:85. K plus premium, with no financing.
  7. a7:2. Choose 2; the model deliberately omits tails, dependence and changing distributions.
  8. a8:1. Same generator, seed and assumptions reproduce the exact paths.

Save an evidence card10min

Write method/assumptions,one reproducible calculation with units,one material limitation and a specific revision. At least30characters in each of method,check and limit. Rubric:explicit model/timing;arithmetic including all cash flows;honest limits;response to feedback. Prose is self-reviewed,not automatically graded. Keep completed lessons,two compared trials,a hand-check and independent-attempt log with your card.

Optional Python consolidation30minutes:two standard-library scripts;separate progress and additional setup time.

Primary references and limits

  • USACE: Monte Carlo workflow, assumed inputs and aggregation
  • Options Industry Council: long call payoff, premium and break-even
  • MIT Finance Theory I: forwards, futures and options teaching sequence

Primary sources checked31October2026. All numerical examples and datasets are original synthetic teaching material. No market profitability claim. Full screen-reader testing and a learner pilot remain pending.
